_: Phase 3 (I-18, I-04): words that switched on the wrong skill. Found by listing every skill found on the 4 test CVs with the exact words that triggered it. 'drop' removes a spelling from a skill; 'add' gives the skill the longer spellings that are not ambiguous; 'move' hands the spellings to a skill that is really theirs. Nothing here guesses: every line was seen on a real CV.

fix.seen: CV3 · 'Patent Portfolio Management' was read as Financial analysis
CV3 · 'liquid detergent dispensing' was read as Healthcare
CV3 · patent work was filed under Contracts and legal, so the person's main expertise had no skill of its own
CV4 · 'worked with branch managers' was read as Banking
CV4 · 'coordinating with vendors/subcontractors' was read as Construction
CV4 · a bill of materials is a parts list, not a drawing. The spellings move to their own skill below.
CV4 · 'Operating Systems: Windows 10' in the tools list was read as Systems programming
CV4 · naming the Windows version you use is not administering it
CV2 · a grade point average was read as Consignment and VMI
CV2 · helping faculty with 'data collection' was read as Data scraping APIs
CV4 · asking suppliers for quotes is purchasing, not selling
CV4 · a factory Production Coordinator was read as media production
CV1 and CV3 · the single word 'organized' was enough to claim the skill
CV4 · the word 'deadlines' alone was enough
CV1 · a school visit to see how 'un projet immobilier' is designed was read as real estate brokerage: the bare word 'immobilier' was a spelling of the skill
CV4 · the employer's name (Purolator) was read as a skill. Company names are not skills (I-04).

new.why: CV3 · the person's main work (patents, prior art, novelty search, freedom to operate) had no skill of its own, so none of it was found (I-19)
CV4 · BOM purchasing is a real skill of its own; it used to be filed under Technical drawings

note_budgeting: The skill named 'Budgeting' also holds every cost-management spelling (cost reduction, cost estimation, cost analysis). It is not a wrong match, but the name shown to the person is wrong: it should read 'Budgeting and cost management'. Renaming touches the related and inferred tables, so it is left for phase 5, where the score and the cards change anyway.

falseFriends._: I-20: these words are written the same in French and in English but mean something else, so on their own they prove nothing. They are never a match by themselves; inside a phrase they still count, because the other words settle the meaning. Seen on CV4: the posting's 'ventes au detail' (retail sales) matched 'attention to details'.

general._: Phase 5 (I-09): skills that nearly every posting asks for and nearly every CV has. They are real skills, but matching on them says little about whether this person fits this job, so they count about a third of a specific skill (MRP, SolidWorks, PLC). They are still shown as a Match.
